children: shares fell 21% on Wednesday after the company reported second quarter results that fell short of Wall Street expectations.
by roughly $1.2M. More importantly, $0.9M of the increase came from the consolidated Health IT business.
The company generated revenues of $3M from teleradiology services, $1M from AI and software solutions, and $0.2M from the sale of imaging systems and OEM services.

Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $11.3M from $10.4M in Q2 2025 and adjusted net loss to $11.6M from $10.9M. The increase in net loss was mainly attributable to the impairment charge related to certain intangible assets, as described above.

The bigger concern is liquidity. Cash fell from $60M as of December 31, 2025 to $31.4M as of June 30, 2026. Post-quarter-end, Nano-X raised aggregate gross proceeds of $8.5M from a registered-direct offering and at-the-market program. The company said it plans to continue raising funds from various sources to strengthen its balance sheet and support its activities.

“To date there has been tangible progress in our commercialization strategy. We have expanded our U.S. distribution footprint to ten partners and begun patient scanning at our first Nanox Imaging Network site in Philadelphia. We have begun receiving reimbursement for scans from insurers for our NIN business. At the same time, Nanox.AI is gaining commercial traction from our new agreement with Vertec Scientific in the UK,” said Erez Meltzer, acting chairman and chief executive officer.

“We have also implemented a multi-pronged cost reduction initiative that includes the restructuring of our South Korea operations, and have raised additional capital to support our operations. We remain focused on disciplined execution as we move systems from our sales pipeline into active clinical use.”

title: Nano-X Imaging stock drops after Q2 loss widens
